cases.title: Pool Nation FX
cases.evidenceSummary: Directly fetched the game's own official PlayStation Store product page (product code contains "POOLNATIONFX"); publisher/developer credited as "Cherry Pop Games Limited" (self-published), no physical-edition branding or messaging anywhere on the listing. Cross-checked retail/marketplace (eBay) and PriceCharting for a boxed PS4 release specifically for "Pool Nation FX" -- found none; every physical/boxed listing that surfaced belongs to the differently-titled, differently-published "Pool Nation" (#922, Wired Productions), confirming the two are not the same product. This is a positive finding (a fetched, self-published digital storefront listing plus a consistent, multi-angle absence of physical evidence), not mere search silence, so it clears the "search silence is not proof" bar.
cases.notConfusedWith: Pool Nation (#922) -- separately published by Wired Productions with its own confirmed physical PS4 release. Untouched by this change; remains its own INCLUDED identity.
cases.ownershipImpact: None -- not present in Josh's GameEye collection.
cases.censusChange: Flipped INCLUDED -> EXCLUDED via census-integrity-pass-v002.js, using the existing find/ensureExcluded convention (same as v001 and ownership-reconcile-v071.js). No alias needed (never owned, no ownership to preserve).

cases.title: 3D Mini Golf / 3D MiniGolf
cases.reason: Same underlying game, republished under two publisher deals.
cases.evidenceSummary: Compared both listings directly against the task's checklist: developer -- identical (Z-Software GmbH) for both. Publisher -- different ("3D Mini Golf" via familyplay, "3D MiniGolf" via Merge Games), which is what made this genuinely ambiguous in the prior pass. Content -- identical: both official PS Store descriptions independently state "over 54 challenging holes, 18 of which are faithfully modeled after official courses in the real world", identical three scenarios (a park, a mountain camping site, a sandy beach), identical Challenge + Tournament modes, identical 1-4 player multiplayer. This is word-for-word matching marketing copy across two nominally-separate storefront listings from different publishers -- the classic pattern of a small developer licensing the same finished game to multiple regional/budget publishing labels (each of whom then submits their own separate PSN product listing and IGDB entry under a near-identical title), not evidence of two different games. This directly explains why IGDB independently has two separate entries both named "3D MiniGolf" (already observed in the earlier cover-curation pass as a TIED_MATCH).
cases.whatChangedSincePriorPass: The prior compilation/census audit (PR #26) flagged this as CURATOR_REVIEW specifically because finding two different publishers looked like it could mean two different products. This pass's direct content comparison (course count, scenarios, modes) resolves that ambiguity -- the content match is exact, not approximate.
cases.canonicalChoice: "3D MiniGolf" (#10) kept as canonical -- it already carries its own automated IGDB cover match from the fetch-covers.mjs pipeline (unlike #9, whose only cover was a manual override reusing #10's art in the first place).
cases.ownershipImpact: None -- neither identity is present in Josh's GameEye collection.
cases.censusChange: "3D Mini Golf" (#9) flipped INCLUDED -> EXCLUDED via census-integrity-pass-v002.js; alias "3d mini golf" added to #10 so any future GameEye import or search under either title resolves to the canonical identity.
cases.coverChange: The prior manual cover-overrides.js entry for #9 (added when this was still an open question, reusing #10's cover) is removed -- #9 is no longer a rendered completion identity, so the override was dead weight. #10's own cover is untouched.
